speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I see you are experiencing intense itching and red bumps on your thigh and elsewhere. To help me understand your condition, how long have these symptoms been present, and have they appeared suddenly or gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with intense itching of his right thigh region for the past few days. He also mentions the recent formation of ‘red bumps’ in the same area. The patient has recently attended a business conference in Miami. He has a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes type 2, and hyperlipidemia. The patient’s medication regimen includes enalapril, metformin, and atorvastatin. He denies any history of smoking or drinking.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Scabies.

The history of intense itching on the thigh, presence of red bumps, recent travel to Miami, and use of atorvastatin (which can cause pruritus) raises suspicion for scabies or drug-induced rash. Given the distribution and intensity, would you say anyone close to you is also experiencing similar itching or skin changes?
